For there it was composed, and from there came the storehouse of all wickedness and blasphemy, the so-called Tome, that is, Leo's letter.
For this reason, from now on God rightly says to them, “I will no longer be with you, because there is something under the ban among you.
The Israelites can no longer stand against their enemies until what is under the ban is removed from among them.”
Let us therefore fear that, through this transgression committed at the council of Chalcedon, the prophecy uttered by the apostle is being fulfilled:
I mean the rebellion after which the coming of the Antichrist follows.
This is what the blessed Timothy, the invincible champion of the true faith, that pillar of orthodoxy, guardian and teacher, the bishop of Alexandria, said.
He spoke, acted, and confirmed things through the Spirit of God, saying plainly: “This is the persecution in which the apostolic saying is fulfilled:
when the dominion of the Roman Empire is abolished—something that has never happened in Rome since it began to reign, until now,
when it committed a great sin: impiety against God and denial of him, and the guide to impiety, the so-called Tome of Leo, which came from it,
as we now see and recognize.” The apostle’s entire prophecy appears as follows in the second letter to the Thessalonians:
“We appeal to you, my brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering to him, that you not be quickly shaken in your understanding,
nor be alarmed, whether by a word, a spirit, or a letter supposedly from us, allegedly concerning the love of our Lord. Let no one deceive you in any way.
For unless the rebellion comes first and the man of sin is revealed, the son of destruction,
the adversary who exalts himself above everything called a god or an object of worship, so that he sits in God’s temple, presenting himself as God.
Do you not remember that when I was still with you, I used to tell you these things? And now you know who restrains him, so that he may be revealed at his appointed time.
For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work. Only when the one who now restrains is removed from the midst, then the lawless one will be revealed.
Our Lord Jesus will destroy him with the breath of his mouth and bring him to nothing by the manifestation of his coming. For that one’s coming is through the working of Satan,
with every kind of power, signs, and false wonders, and with all this deception. God will send them a working of deception, so that they will believe the lie,
so that all who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in lawlessness may be condemned.”
For the statement, “The mystery of lawlessness has already begun to run rampant; only when the one who now restrains is removed from the midst,”
was said in a veiled way about the abolition of the Roman Empire, according to the holy fathers and teachers. Who, then, will be found blessed and three times blessed,
being thus also firm in faith, fervent in spirit, ready for every kind of endurance, and possessing the confidence to be able to make that apostolic boast which says:
“I have fought the good fight, finished my race, and kept my faith. From now on the crown of righteousness is reserved for me, which our Lord will award me on that day,
for he is the righteous judge.” He goes on to say: “And not only to me, but also to all who have loved his appearing.”
For then the prophecy of the prophet Zechariah will be fulfilled decisively and unmistakably, which says: “There will no longer be anything accursed, nor any Canaanite in the house of the Lord.”
This is the Council of Chalcedon, its wicked faith, and its new decree.
This is the final unclean sign, the accursed thing, and the forerunner of the Antichrist, together with those who share its secrets and agree with it in their thinking,
these cursed and rejected Canaanites, as we have shown in the things written above.
There are also other testimonies, demonstrations, and assurances that come from God, particularly to the saints and generally to all human beings.
Concerning the transgression that took place at the Council of Chalcedon. But, so as not to make this writing too long, I think these things are sufficient for faithful hearers.
For those who love God receive well these things that have been set down with complete truthfulness.
For we must give an account to him who is to judge the living and the dead justly. He is the exacting judge who knows hearts, the God of truth.
And therefore this is good. In this too, observe the apostle’s instruction to Timothy: “You, then, my son, be strengthened by the grace that is in Jesus Christ.
And the things you have heard from me through many witnesses, entrust to faithful people who are capable of teaching others as well.”
For Saint Basil says that casting the mystery of reverence for God among the unworthy is like pouring costly perfumed oil into a filthy vessel.
An apostolic command. “Fight the good fight of faith. Take hold of eternal life, to which you were called and for which you made the good confession
before many witnesses. O Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you, avoiding empty and profane talk
and the contradictions of false knowledge. By professing it, some have fallen away from the truth. Grace be with you. Amen.”
Here end the assurances, testimonies, and revelations that came from God through the saints concerning the heresy of the two natures and the transgression that took place at Chalcedon.
These accounts, which Saint John, the disciple of Abba Peter the Iberian, the holy bishop, carefully collected,
I have placed here to show how much destruction was brought about by the Council of Chalcedon, which took place through Satan’s activity. Again, concerning a monk who was a deacon.
In the city of Edessa there was a church of Saint John the Baptist,
who is renowned even to this day for working miracles. There was a custom in this enviable city,
observed there for a long time, that anyone suffering from pain in the eyes would go to that church and seek refuge there to obtain relief.
Now, four years before the present time, there was a man originally from the city of Amida,
a chaste monk who was being trained in the holy monastery of the Easterners in Edessa and was a deacon. He was afflicted with this suffering
and pain in his eyes, which had already been somewhat weak beforehand. He went out to that church and stayed there a day and a night, but the pain grew worse,
so that he reached utter despair [?]. In his anguish of heart, he wanted to throw himself into a well near the church. As he passed through the doorway to go there,
the blessed John the Baptist himself met him and asked him, “What do you intend to do?” The deacon said, “I am going to throw myself into the well.”
The saint said to him, “Do not be distressed, and do not do yourself any harm.” Passing his hand over his face, he said to him, “Go to that washing place
and wash, and you will be healed. But do not look for me in this church, because I am not in it, since the Chalcedonians took it over.
I no longer enter it. Because they defiled it, I have departed from it.” Then the deacon did as the saint had said, and he was healed.
Do not doubt these things or say that they are fabrications and lies, for I tell you, as before God,
that the very people to whom these things happened recounted them before many people.
And you too, our brother, must not doubt these things, but accept them with complete conviction and confidence.
Let us pray that we may preserve this faith we hold until our last breath. Let each of us persuade himself to live in a way that accords with the faith.
If we do this, we will be counted worthy of the kingdom of heaven, through the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ. To him, his Father, and his Holy Spirit be glory forever and ever. Amen.
Another account of something that happened in Sebaste in Palestine, where the body of John the Baptist lies.
At the time of the detestable and wicked Council of Chalcedon, there was a caretaker serving in that place, the blessed Constantine,
who delighted every day in seeing the Baptist and the prophet Elisha, and in the freedom of speech he enjoyed with Saint John.
When the oppression and persecution associated with Chalcedon began, and the bishops ordained by Patriarch Athanasius were driven out by the wicked Marcian, he was troubled in his thoughts.
If he fled from communion with the deniers of the faith, he would be deprived of his fellowship with Saint John the Baptist; but if he stayed, he would become a transgressor.
He implored the Forerunner to reveal to him what would please God and benefit him. The Baptist said to him, “Priest, do not destroy yourself and deny your faith for my sake.
Leave and keep your faith uncorrupted. Wherever you go, I am with you.” So the priest left and remained blameless in exile.
Another account. The holy, God-fearing Rhosius, an exile and a chaste man, was also granted such reassurance and spiritual encouragement, and a vision.
While he was living in a cell on Mount Sinai, he set out and came to Jerusalem, seeking a quiet place. He reached Bethel,
where Jacob the patriarch saw the ladder. The caretaker of that place became fond of him and urged him insistently to stay, promising him
that he would provide him with suitable comforts. He openly declared, “I cannot do this, because I am fleeing from the communion and denial of the faith associated with Chalcedon.”
The caretaker said to him with oaths, “We will put no pressure at all on you about this. Just stay with me and sing psalms with me.”
In his simplicity, his mind inclined toward this proposal. That night he saw the patriarch Jacob, a white-haired man, dignified and austere,
wrapped in a cloak, holding a staff, and walking about that place. He approached him and said, “How is it that you, being orthodox,

are sharing communion with deniers of the faith and wish to live here for a long time? Do not transgress against your faith for my sake. Instead, take care and flee from communion with deniers of the faith,
and you will lack nothing good.” By fleeing, he was preserved in the orthodox faith until the end.
Another account. As soon as the orthodox are driven from their churches, the Holy Spirit departs with them,
and the adversary enters with the heretics. To confirm this matter, we have recounted a few examples out of many before our listeners.
A holy and trustworthy man related that there was a holy martyr in the region of the Thebaid who performed miracles and mighty works.
Many sick people, people possessed by demons, and people with leprosy would come to his church, and he would appear to them face to face.
After some time, the heretics seized his church. He would appear on the roads to the sick people who were coming to his monastery and say to them,
“I am Marcellus the martyr, to whom you are going. Do not go there any longer. I am not there; I have moved away.”
For those who deny God have defiled my house; I will no longer be seen there. These things are enough for believers.
